summary: The count of double-envelope ballots is still under way, and the partial tally shows no shift between the blocs: Netanyahu's camp leads but lacks a majority, with Eisenkot's camp further behind. Netanyahu now says no Zionist party can partner with Ra'am or the Joint List in light of the foreign-interference allegations, which Arab party leaders and Qatar deny and election officials say they cannot confirm. On the other side, Golan met Lapid to coordinate, Liberman repeated that he won't sit with Netanyahu, the Joint List or the Haredi parties, and Channel 12 reports UTJ sources are floating outside support for an Eisenkot government in exchange for draft concessions. President Herzog will consult the factions once official results are published, expected Nov 4.

phase.now: Double-envelope ballots still being counted (about 296,000 of up to 480,000 tallied by mid-afternoon Oct 29)
phase.next: The Central Elections Committee expects the full count on the evening of Oct 29 and official results on Nov 4; Herzog then consults every faction before choosing who gets the first try at forming a government.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners, whom he told they are staying together. Without a majority, Netanyahu needs defectors or a new partner from the other side.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu rather than join him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Proposed by Yair Golan, who meets Eisenkot and Lapid separately on Oct 29, with Abbas and the Joint List both offering help. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Abbas says both camps have contacted him, but this falls short of 61 even before Liberman's veto.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it in two. Channel 12 reports UTJ sources are proposing a looser variant: backing an Eisenkot government from outside by skipping votes, in exchange for draft concessions; no response from Eisenkot was reported.

blockers.text: A Shas official told Ynet that Deri won't leave Netanyahu's bloc or negotiate with Eisenkot.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman repeated on Oct 29 that he won't sit in a government with the Haredi parties.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ, while anonymous change-bloc sources dismiss the idea. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point.

blockers.text: Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: Netanyahu says that, given the interference allegations, no Zionist party can partner with Ra'am or the Joint List; Likud says the election was stolen.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of using an unfinished interference probe to undermine the election results and insists the new Knesset convene on time, while still refusing to serve under him.

רק.stance: Bennett says 'Netanyahu has lost' and that talks among opposition leaders are underway.

אמת.stance: Golan met Lapid as part of an effort to oust Netanyahu and says the two will keep working in tandem; he still favors partnering with the Arab parties.

ל.stance: Liberman called the Shin Bet request dramatic and unprecedented and repeated that he won't sit with Netanyahu, the Joint List or the Haredi parties; Channel 12 says he is avoiding his allies' calls.

שס.stance: A Shas official says Deri won't leave Netanyahu's bloc or negotiate with Eisenkot; Shas still demands a draft-exemption law.

ג.stance: Asher mocked the opposition's 'alliance of those who serve' label; separately, Channel 12 reports unnamed UTJ sources floating outside support for an Eisenkot government in exchange for draft concessions.

ב.stance: Ben-Gvir calls the interference allegations a "political October 7" and wants Arab party leaders arrested if there are legal grounds; he rejects unity with Eisenkot.

ט.stance: Smotrich says the Arab party heads should be questioned by the Shin Bet over the alleged foreign funding; no coalition terms stated yet.

עם.stance: Abbas denies any link to the alleged foreign interference, pledges full cooperation with investigators and accuses Netanyahu of inciting against Arab citizens; he has said he'd join a government that tackles crime and discrimination.

ודם.stance: The Joint List calls the interference accusations racist lies and says it won't apologize for its results; it remains ready to help oust Netanyahu.
